guide.h2: What a decorating quote should include
ul: Which rooms and surfaces: walls, ceilings, woodwork, doors and radiators
Preparation: filling cracks, sanding, sugar soaping and caulking gaps
Mist coats on new plaster, which needs thinned paint before the top coats
The number of coats and the paint brand and finish
Protecting floors and furniture, and clearing up each day
Whether paint and materials are included in the price

guide.h2: Preparation is most of the job
p: A good painter and decorator spends more time on preparation than on painting. Cracks are filled and sanded, old gloss is keyed so new paint sticks, and gaps around skirting and frames are caulked. If you have just had a room plastered, the plaster needs to dry fully before painting. See plasterers in Leeds if the walls need work first.

Exterior work, such as painting rendered walls, fascias, window frames and doors, depends on dry weather and usually runs from spring to early autumn in Leeds. Interior decorating can be done all year. If you need scaffolding for high exterior work, ask whether it is included in the quote.

Spraying or hand painting kitchen cupboards can make a dated kitchen look new for a fraction of the cost of replacement. It needs careful cleaning, keying and the right primer, or the paint will chip. Ask to see photos of kitchens the decorator has done before.

Many decorators also hang wallpaper, from lining paper to patterned feature walls. Patterned paper takes longer to hang because the pattern has to match at every join, so expect the price to reflect that.

guide.h2: Finding a painter and decorator in Leeds
p: Ask two or three painters and decorators in Leeds for a free quote after they have seen the rooms. Most local decorators cover Leeds and the surrounding areas, and some work further across West Yorkshire and up to Harrogate. Look for excellent reviews that mention the same kind of painting and decorating project as yours, whether that is interior painting, exterior painting, wallpaper or a full house. A professional painter and decorator should be happy to show you recent work and explain how they will sand, fill and prepare before painting.

faqs.q: How long does it take to paint a room?
faqs.a: A typical bedroom or living room takes one to two days, including preparation, two coats on the walls and the woodwork. Larger rooms, high ceilings and lots of preparation take longer.

faqs.q: Should the decorator supply the paint?
faqs.a: Either works. Decorators often get trade prices on paint, but if you want a particular brand or colour, agree it in writing before work starts.

faqs.q: When can you paint new plaster?
faqs.a: Only once it has dried fully, which can take several days to a few weeks depending on the thickness and the weather. The first coat should be a mist coat of thinned emulsion.

faqs.q: Do painters and decorators work in winter?
faqs.a: Yes, inside. Exterior painting needs dry weather above freezing, so most outside work in Leeds is booked from spring to early autumn.
